newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN recommends six-month renewal of Georgia mission.
newsitem.headline: UN recommends six-month renewal of Georgia mission.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan recommended on Wednesday a six-month renewal, until July 31, of the 125-member U.N. Observer Mission in Georgia (UNOMIG), where negotiations between the government and Abkhaz separatists have made little progress.
About 250,000 Georgians fled the Abkhazia region, near the Black Sea, in 1993 when separatists backed by mercenaries and arms from Russia's northern Caucasus drove out Georgian government troops.
Occasional violence has since punctuated an uneasy calm enforced by Russian-led peacekeepers fielded by the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).

The latest U.N. report said key issues on the future political status of Abkhazia and the return of refugees were unresolved. But the parties themselves had begun to revitalise the peace process by meeting bilaterally at high levels.

"The role of the United Nations at present should be to support the efforts of the two sides to arrive at mutually acceptable compromises that would underpin an overall settlement," the secretary-general said.
The United Nations intended initiating contacts in the region soon to assist the two sides "in their apparent attempt to unblock the peace process," he added.

Referring to continuing acts of violence by armed groups, he called on all parties to "take effective measures to end a situation that can only have negative effects for the return of peace to the region."
